GBR.name: United Kingdom, c.1945–65
GBR.note: Nationalisation of 'commanding heights' under Attlee without a binding plan; Treasury-led demand management; indicative planning only from the National Economic Development Council (1962). Colonies held sterling balances in the Sterling Area through currency boards.

FRA.name: France, c.1946–65
FRA.note: Indicative planning through the Commissariat général du Plan (Monnet Plan, 1946); FIDES funds carried planned investment to the colonies; franc zone and CFA franc (1945).

PRT.name: Portugal, c.1953–74
PRT.note: Estado Novo corporatism with Planos de Fomento (from 1953) covering metropole and overseas provinces; escudo zone.

NLD.name: Netherlands, c.1945–62
NLD.note: Centraal Planbureau (1945, Tinbergen): macroeconomic forecasting and policy advice rather than directive plans; guilder-linked colonial currencies.

SUN.name: Soviet model
SUN.note: Gosplan five-year plans, state ownership, non-convertible currency, bloc trade.

USA.name: United States / Bretton Woods model
USA.note: Market allocation with project-based aid; after 1980 the World Bank and IMF adjustment agenda (liberalised trade and prices, floating or flexible exchange rates).

AGO.name: Angola

lineage.summary: Independence in war; the MPLA adopted Marxism-Leninism and central planning with Soviet and Cuban support, alongside an oil enclave.

notes.text: MPLA First Congress declares a Marxist-Leninist programme.
notes.src: MPLA (1977) Orientações Fundamentais

notes.text: Programa de Saneamento Económico e Financeiro begins the market turn.
notes.src: Government of Angola (1987) SEF

sources: La Porta et al. (2008) J. Econ. Lit. 46(2)

MPLA First Congress (1977), Marxist-Leninist programme; Programa de Saneamento Económico e Financeiro (1987); market reforms from 1990.

BGD.name: Bangladesh

lineage.summary: Began with nationalisation and a socialist-leaning first plan, then moved under donor influence towards liberalisation.

notes.text: Mass nationalisation of industry and banks after independence.
notes.src: Sobhan, R. and Ahmad, M. (1980) Public Enterprise in an Intermediate Regime

notes.text: First Five Year Plan 1973–78 drafted by the Planning Commission under Nurul Islam.

notes.text: Denationalisation under donor-supported adjustment.

CIV.name: Côte d'Ivoire

lineage.summary: The closest continuation of the French model: indicative plans, French advisers in ministries and the CFA franc.

DZA.name: Algeria

lineage.summary: French planning forms filled with a Soviet-style industrial strategy, designed partly by the French economist Destanne de Bernis.

notes.text: Autogestion (self-management) of abandoned settler estates.
notes.src: March decrees, 1963

notes.text: Triennial and four-year plans built on 'industrialising industries' and hydrocarbons.
notes.src: de Bernis, G. D. (1971) Les industries industrialisantes et les options algériennes, Tiers-Monde 47

notes.text: IMF stand-by and structural adjustment.

GHA.name: Gold Coast / Ghana

lineage.summary: British colonial development plans continued at first; Nkrumah's Seven-Year Plan turned socialist, before IMF-backed recovery in 1983.

GIN.name: Guinea

lineage.summary: The sharpest break with France: a 'No' vote in 1958, exit from the franc zone and a Soviet-bloc planned economy.

notes.text: Guinea rejects the French Community; French personnel withdraw.
notes.src: Referendum of 28 September 1958

notes.text: Own currency outside the franc zone; three-year plan with Eastern-bloc aid.
notes.src: Plan triennal 1960–63

IDN.name: Dutch East Indies / Indonesia

lineage.summary: Little Dutch planning tradition was carried over; Guided Economy planning under Sukarno, then US-trained technocrats under Suharto.

IND.name: British India / India
IND.admin_tradition: direct (with princely states under indirect rule)

lineage.summary: A British administrative and legal frame carrying a planning model borrowed largely from the Soviet Union and from India's own pre-independence plans.

notes.text: The Bombay Plan, drafted by Indian industrialists, already called for state-led heavy industry and planned investment.
notes.src: Thakurdas, P. et al. (1944) A Brief Memorandum Outlining a Plan of Economic Development for India

notes.text: Planning Commission set up under the Prime Minister; the First Five-Year Plan (1951) is largely a public investment programme.
notes.src: Government of India, First Five Year Plan (1952)

notes.text: The Second Plan follows P. C. Mahalanobis's two-sector model, prioritising heavy industry in the Soviet manner.
notes.src: Mahalanobis, P. C. (1955) The approach of operational research to planning in India, Sankhyā 16

notes.text: Balance-of-payments crisis and IMF programme; the Eighth Plan (1992) moves to indicative planning.
notes.src: Government of India, Eighth Five Year Plan (1992)

notes.text: Planning Commission replaced by NITI Aayog, a policy think tank without allocative powers.
notes.src: Government of India Cabinet Resolution, 1 January 2015

sources: Government of India Planning Commission, Second Five Year Plan (1956); Chakravarty, S. (1987) Development Planning: The Indian Experience; NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015.

KEN.name: Kenya
KEN.admin_tradition: indirect (settler colony with direct administration of highlands)

lineage.summary: 'African socialism' in name, a market economy with planning in practice, close to the late-colonial model.

notes.text: Sessional Paper No. 10 defines African socialism while protecting private property and foreign investment.
notes.src: Republic of Kenya (1965) Sessional Paper No. 10

notes.text: World Bank structural adjustment lending.

MMR.name: Burma / Myanmar

lineage.summary: An American-drafted welfare plan in the 1950s, then an inward-looking military socialism of its own design.
